criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml requirement OLY-3-06 has a mechanism naming crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs and the new function (not 'none'), owner 'Athena', and a measure naming the test and ending with 'status: not shown'. Check with Grep on docs/spec.toml.
criteria.evidence: I grepped docs/spec.toml. Lines 482-485 read: mechanism = "crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs: feedback_dimension_counts reports how many ...", owner = "Athena", and measure = "Shown by the test run with cargo test -p athena-core a_dimension_can_hold_several_items; no athena status line prints per-dimension counts; status: not shown".

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core on the new test. It builds a record with several decisions_matched and earlier_cases entries and asserts the per-dimension counts exceed 1 for those dimensions and are 0 for blank ones. The test fails if the function is stubbed to return one per filled dimension.
criteria.evidence: I ran the test and it passed (1 passed). The test sets 3 decisions_matched, 2 earlier_cases and what_happened. It asserts the counts are exactly [1, 3, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] and that n[1] > 1 and n[2] > 1. A stub returning 1 per filled dimension gives [1, 1, 1, 0, ...], which fails both the assert_eq and the > 1 check. I worked this out from the assertions; I did not run a stub, because the verifier may not edit files.

findings.summary: The mapping from fields to dimensions is now written twice, so the two copies can drift apart.
findings.evidence: filled_feedback_dimensions (lines 1693-1712) and feedback_dimension_counts (lines 1717-1731) each list the ten fields in FEEDBACK_DIMENSIONS order and use the same blank-text rule. A simpler fix is to build filled_feedback_dimensions from feedback_dimension_counts (keep the dimensions whose count is above 0), so the order and field choices live in one place.

findings.summary: Only a test calls the mechanism; no production code uses it.
findings.evidence: A grep for feedback_dimension_counts in crates/ finds only the definition and the test. The accepted reading allows this ('Calls to the new function come from tests only'), and the measure honestly says 'status: not shown'. So the requirement is shown by a unit test, not by Athena's own behaviour.

summary: The change meets OLY-3-06 and every acceptance criterion; the verdict is pass. It adds feedback_dimension_counts in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs, which counts how many items an introspection record holds for each of the ten feedback dimensions. The matched decisions and the earlier cases count one per entry; every other dimension counts 0 or 1. docs/spec.toml now records this function as OLY-3-06's mechanism, with owner Athena and a measure that names the test and ends with 'status: not shown'. I ran the new test, a_dimension_can_hold_several_items, and it passed. Its exact assertion of [1, 3, 2, 0, ...] would fail against a stub that returns 1 per filled dimension; I worked that out from the assertions and did not run a stub. Athena's recorded CI checks show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. The three changed files are exactly the expected deliverables. Two minor points remain: the field-to-dimension mapping is now written in two places and could drift (filled_feedback_dimensions could be built from the counts instead), and only a test calls the new function, which the accepted reading allows.
